restrictions.note: No specialist-only or shared-care restriction stated in the SmPC. Fixed-dose combination for patients not controlled on monotherapy (see indications).

items.t: One tablet once daily. Titrate the individual components first (direct switch from monotherapy may be considered). If uncontrolled, increase either component up to a maximum of 320 mg/25 mg. Effect largely within 2 weeks, maximal in about 4 weeks (sometimes 4-8 weeks).

src.q: is one film-coated tablet once daily. Dose titration with the individual components is recommended.
the dose may be increased by increasing either one of the components to a maximum dose of Co-Diovan 320 mg/25 mg

items.t: Angioedema: stop immediately and do not re-administer. Caution with previous hypersensitivity to other ARBs; hydrochlorothiazide hypersensitivity more likely with allergy or asthma.

src.q: Hydrochlorothiazide should not be administered to patients who previously experienced ARDS following hydrochlorothiazide intake.

items.t: Lithium: not recommended (raised lithium levels and toxicity, increased further by the thiazide); if needed, monitor lithium carefully.

src.q: Since renal clearance of lithium is reduced by thiazides, the risk of lithium toxicity may presumably be increased further with Co-Diovan.

items.t: ACE inhibitors, other ARBs, aliskiren: dual RAAS blockade (more hypotension, hyperkalaemia, renal impairment). Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium salt substitutes: not recommended; monitor potassium if needed.

src.q: Concomitant use not recommended Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium and other substances that may increase potassium levels.

items.t: NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors and aspirin above 3 g/day): reduced antihypertensive effect, worsening renal function, raised potassium; monitor renal function at the start and keep hydrated.

src.q: concomitant use of Co-Diovan and NSAIDs may lead to worsening of renal function and an increase in serum potassium
Therefore, monitoring of renal function at the beginning of the treatment is recommended, as well as adequate hydration of the patient.

items.t: Medicines lowering potassium (other diuretics, corticosteroids, laxatives, amphotericin, salicylates): monitor potassium. Torsades-inducing medicines (class Ia/III antiarrhythmics, some antipsychotics): caution because of hypokalaemia. Digoxin: hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia favour arrhythmias.

src.q: If these medicinal products are to be prescribed with the hydrochlorothiazide-valsartan combination, monitoring of potassium plasma levels is advised
hydrochlorothiazide should be administered with caution when associated with medicinal products that could induce torsades de pointes

items.t: Antidiabetics: dose adjustment may be needed; metformin with caution (lactic acidosis with functional renal failure). Beta-blockers: more hyperglycaemia. Allopurinol: more hypersensitivity reactions. Calcium salts or vitamin D: serum calcium may rise.

items.t: Antidepressants, antipsychotics, antiepileptics: may intensify hyponatraemia; caution in long-term use. Methotrexate and other cytotoxics: reduced renal excretion, more myelosuppression. Colestyramine/colestipol: give hydrochlorothiazide at least 4 h before or 4-6 h after.
